title: What Cave Hotel Networks Is
definition: Cave Hotel Networks: networks of hotels in caves.
description:
Cave Hotel Networks: networks of hotels in caves. This is Future Architecture & Building at its most ambitious — cave suites research, network logistics engineering and humidity control operations converging on a single goal: making network hulls real.

Why it matters: Future Architecture & Building will decide lighting design outcomes this century. Cave Hotel Networks is one of the load-bearing ideas: without working network hulls, the larger cave suites vision stalls, and with it, the network logistics systems that depend on it.

This database documents Cave Hotel Networks in full: what it is, the real research behind it today, the pieces it is built from, dated forecasts, runnable demo programs, and a teaching ladder from foundations to mastery. Every record carries a working program you can run.

t: Real Research Today: Cave Hotel Networks
title: Real Research Today: Cave Hotel Networks
definition: Today's documented research behind Cave Hotel Networks.
description:
The road to Cave Hotel Networks is already being paved. Earthship and passive-house movements prove ultra-low-energy building. Robotics in construction (Built Robotics, Dusty Robotics) automates layout and earthworks.

Mass timber towers (Mjøstårnet Norway, Ascent Milwaukee) prove tall wood buildings. Together these programs form the cave suites foundation that Cave Hotel Networks will build on — the network logistics results, the humidity control methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as network logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: 2030 — First network hulls districts certified: cave suites assembly at
definition: 2030 milestone on the Cave Hotel Networks roadmap.
description:
First network hulls districts certified: cave suites assembly at half the time and carbon of legacy builds.

What must be true first: the cave suites results have to replicate outside the lab, network logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and humidity control operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed cave suites demonstrations, network logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting humidity control uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Cave Hotel Networks
definition: Estimates Cave Hotel Networks readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Cave Hotel Networks components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a network hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Cave Hotel Networks Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Cave Hotel Networks operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Cave Hotel Networks installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 86861 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where cave suites monitoring, network logistics redundancy, or humidity control maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Cave Hotel Networks Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Cave Hotel Networks: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Cave Hotel Networks — networks of hotels in caves.

Phase 1 — Prove (cave suites): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (network logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (humidity control): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (lighting design): network hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and tourism-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
